text: At 79', Westport Albion triggered a tactical shift focused on protecting their 3-2 lead by dropping their defensive line and reducing pressing intensity—PPDA rose from 4.5 to 5.5—while decreasing their tempo by 0.35 to slow play [#1459]. This rest-defense mechanism aimed to absorb Kingsmoor FC’s wide, crossing 4-4-2 attacks by conceding more possession (field tilt rose slightly from 30.8% to 32.0%) and increased opponent xG from 0 to 0.94, reflecting a controlled trade-off for defensive solidity [#1459]. Westport’s minimization of turnovers (from 5 to 0 high turnovers) and balanced box touches indicate measured ball retention in low-risk zones, consistent with their direct vertical passing style adapted to a deeper posture late in the match [#1459]. Despite a reduction in their own xG from 0.37 to 0.26, this strategic slowdown effectively prioritized safeguarding the lead through cautious positional discipline rather than pressing triggers or overloads.
